contracts.grain: One row per broker (trimmed, upper-cased broker code, with DIRECT for policies that have no broker) and line of business that has any in-force policies, written premium, notified claims or paid claims in the year up to the as-of date.

columns.name: broker_code
columns.description: Trimmed and upper-cased. 'DIRECT' when the policy snapshot has no broker.

columns.name: broker_name
columns.description: NULL when the broker code is not in stg.brokers (for example DIRECT).

columns.name: broker_status
columns.description: Upper-cased status from stg.brokers. NULL when the broker is not found.

columns.name: policies_in_force
columns.description: Number of policies whose latest snapshot on or before the as-of date is in force on that date.

columns.name: gwp_eur
columns.description: Premium booked from 1 January to the as-of date, converted to EUR at the latest FX rate published on or before the transaction date.

columns.name: claims_notified
columns.description: Claims reported in the year up to the as-of date.

columns.name: claims_paid_eur
columns.description: Payments made in the year on claims notified in the year, with recoveries netted off and NULL amounts ignored.

columns.name: paid_to_written
columns.description: Broker-level ratio over all of the broker's lines, so the same value repeats on each of the broker's rows. NULL when the broker's total premium is zero.

columns.name: review_flag
columns.description: 'Y' when the broker-level paid_to_written is above 0.75, otherwise 'N' (including when the ratio is NULL).

cases.description: Line 58: the snapshots carry product_code in different cases ('mot01', 'Mot01', 'hom01', 'pRODUCT' style), but stg.products only has upper-case codes. Under the CI collation, SQL Server joins all of them, so they count in policies_in_force. A binary Spark join drops them. Policies 1, 4 and 6 are the upper-case controls.

Line 58: some snapshot product_codes carry trailing spaces ('MOT01 ', 'MOT01  ', 'HOM01 '), and one products row is stored as 'PET01 ' while its snapshot says 'PET01'. SQL Server ignores the trailing spaces, so every policy joins. A Spark equality without rtrim loses policies 2, 3, 5 and 6. Policies 1 and 4 are the unpadded controls.

Line 76: premium transactions in currency 'eur', 'Eur' and 'eUR'. Under CI, they match currency = 'EUR' and are taken at a factor of 1. fx_rates also holds an EUR rate of 1.1. A binary CASE sends these rows to the fx lookup, where they either find no rate (the premium becomes NULL and drops out) or get the 1.1 rate. Either way gwp_eur changes. The 'EUR' and 'GBP' rows are controls.

Line 76: currency is CHAR(3), so a full 'EUR' cannot also carry a trailing space within the column length. The case uses padded short codes instead: 'US ' and 'GB ' are compared against 'EUR' in the CASE and then go to the fx lookup, where fx_rates has 'US' and 'GB' without padding. The 'EUR' rows are controls, and fx_rates holds an EUR rate of 1.1 so that any EUR row wrongly sent to the fx rate shows up. A Spark comparison that does not trim padded CHAR values does not match these rows the way SQL Server does.

Line 76: amount DECIMAL(12,2) times rate DECIMAL(18,8), summed per broker and LOB. For BRK001/MOTOR, 0.50*1.001 plus 0.50*1.009 sums to exactly 1.005. For BRK001/HOME, three 333.33*0.33333333 pieces sum to 333.3299966667. The other rows use high-scale rates and a negative adjustment. If the math is done in double, sums like 1.005 drift below the half and round to 1.00 instead of the decimal 1.01.

Lines 81-85: fx_rates has two GBP rows dated 2025-03-01 (1.15, then 1.17) and two USD rows dated 2025-03-01 (0.90, then 0.92). The TOP 1 picks the row with the higher _row_seq on the tied date. There is also a GBP rate dated after one transaction, which must not be used, and an earlier GBP rate for a February transaction. A Spark window that does not break ties by _row_seq DESC, or uses a non-deterministic first(), can pick the wrong rate.

Line 83: the transaction currencies 'gbp' and 'Gbp' must match fx 'GBP', and transaction 'USD' must match fx rows stored as 'Usd' and 'usd'. Under CI, SQL Server finds the latest rate for each. A binary Spark match finds no rate, so the premium is NULL and those groups get gwp 0. The 'GBP' and 'EUR' rows are controls.

Line 83: CHAR(3) padded short codes. Transaction 'GB ' must match fx 'GB', transaction 'GB' must match the later fx 'GB ' row, and transaction 'US' must match fx 'US '. SQL Server ignores the trailing spaces and finds the rate. An exact Spark match finds none, so the premium is NULL. The 'GBP' and 'EUR' rows are controls.

Line 124: the broker-level paid/written ratio sits right at the 0.75 threshold. BRK001: 15000.99/20000 = 0.7500495, which is rounded to 6dp by the division and then to 4dp by the cast. BRK002: 7500.01/10000 = 0.750001, which rounds to 0.7500, so the flag is N even though the raw value is above 0.75. BRK003 spans two LOBs, 7500.50/10000 = 0.75005, which rounds half up to 0.7501, so Y. BRK004 is exactly 0.75. A null payment and a payment after the as-of date are excluded. A double or unrounded ratio flips the flags.

Line 142: each group's high-scale gwp lands exactly on a half cent. 1.00*1.125 = 1.125 should give 1.13, -1.00*1.125 = -1.125 should give -1.13 (half away from zero), 5.00*1.125 = 5.625 should give 5.63, and 3.00*1.165 = 3.495 and 1.00*1.165 = 1.165 should give 3.50 and 1.17. Banker's rounding or rounding through a double gives 1.12, -1.12, 5.62, 3.49 and 1.16. The EUR group is the control.

Line 144: claims paid summed as decimal. Claim 1 has ten payments of 0.10, which sum to 0.9999999999999999 in double. Claim 2 has 100.00, a -25.50 recovery and a NULL amount. Claim 3 has three payments of 1.15, which sum to 3.4499999999999997 in double. Decimal gives exactly 1.00 and 3.45. Double plus truncation or a cast can give 0.99 and 3.44. Claim 4 has no payments, and claim 5 was reported in 2024 and is excluded.

Line 148: the report key broker_code is trimmed and upper-cased, but stg.brokers stores 'brk001', 'Brk002', 'bRK003' and 'direct'. Under CI, SQL Server joins them and fills broker_name and status. A binary Spark join leaves both NULL. BRK004 is the exact-match control. Policy 2's snapshot code is lower case, and policy 4 has a NULL broker_code, which becomes DIRECT.

Line 148: brokers.broker_code is CHAR(6) and holds space-padded values ('BRK01 ', 'BRK2  ', 'AB    ', 'DIRECT') that must match the trimmed keys 'BRK01', 'BRK2' and 'AB'. Policy 2's snapshot code ' BRK2 ' is trimmed in the key. SQL Server ignores the trailing spaces and fills broker_name and status. A Spark join without rtrim on b.broker_code leaves them NULL. BRK003 and DIRECT are full-width controls.
